dates.chronologyKeyBasis: Will dated 31 March 1714, proved 30 April 1714; Sarah died 16 April 1714 in the interval.
dates.display: will 31 March 1714; Sarah d. 16 April 1714; proved 30 April 1714

outgoing.explanation: The 1714 will and inventory is direct primary evidence closing out the Providence household and its lack of Gurney offspring.

shortLabel: 1714 Providence will and inventory of Sarah Gurney; husband John Gurney alive

sources.locator: Early Records of the Town of Providence: council meeting image 220 (ark WS3H-N); will/attestation image 412 (ark GSPG-8); inventory/death-date image 414 (ark GSPP-T); executor bond, Providence Probate Records image 392 (ark 3Q9M-C95S-Q9DR-L)

statement: Sarah Gurney of Providence died 16 April 1714; her will of 31 March 1714, proved 30 April 1714, names her husband John Gurney as still living — he witnessed the will and co-appraised the inventory by mark — and leaves everything to her children by a prior marriage, all surnamed Field.
